text:
The Wild have points in eight straight (6-0-2), and the run looks earned: 57 percent of the expected goals in those games. Saturday's 4-3 overtime loss to Tampa Bay, after leading 3-1 in the third, was a rare bad night in a very good month.

Kirill Kaprizov leads the league with 16 goals, and the line he shares with Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy has done something absurd: 16 goals for, zero against, in 201 minutes together at five on five. That won't stay at zero, but 65 percent of the expected goals says it's mostly real. Quinn Hughes, a pending 2027 free agent per Daily Faceoff's list, has driven both of his pairs to 57 percent of the chances or better, and he's been telling reporters there's "zero selfishness" in the room.

Then there's Jesper Wallstedt, who has saved 5.4 goals above expected over his last five starts, with Yahoo already calling him the Vezina front-runner. Maxim Shabanov, with three goals in two nights, gives them a second line that can finish. One honest flag: Minnesota's goalies have stopped about 11 more goals than expected over the season, and the shooters have scored about seven fewer. Those two roughly cancel, which is why our simulations still put them at 98 percent for the playoffs.
headline: Minnesota has a superstar line and a Vezina case in net
